subject: common raven
title: Ravens Find Wolf Kills 90 Miles Away Without Following the Wolves

scenes.text: Ravens find wolf kills without following the wolves.
People long assumed ravens tailed wolf packs to steal their scraps.
So scientists put GPS tags on sixty-nine ravens and twenty wolves in Yellowstone.
In two and a half years, they found just one clear case of a raven following a wolf.
Instead, ravens remember where kills usually happen, and fly straight there, some over ninety miles in a day.
They're not following the hunters. They're reading the map.

description:
A 2026 Science study tracked 69 GPS-tagged ravens and 20 collared wolves in Yellowstone for two and a half years. Only one raven clearly trailed a wolf for more than a kilometre or an hour.
Instead, ravens return to valleys where kills are common, some flying up to 155 kilometres in a day, apparently from memory.
What's the smartest bird you've ever seen?
first_comment: Some ravens can fly six hours non-stop straight to a kill site, says the study's lead author. Do you think crows and ravens are smarter than dogs?
